register.title: Amund Kristiansen's beyond-horizon certificate at 344, f916f69, issue819
register.headline: Kristiansen's packing at 344, the 307 record design stretched one step, certified exactly below Couzo's
register.source_checks: The author reports that Evan Daniel's two exact rational checkers at evand/square-packing 7982d7a, verify_cert.py (separating axes) and verify_cert2.py (polygon intersection), accept the certificate, with least wall clearance 6.054e-13, least pair separation 1.215e-12 and 794 close pairs, re-checked on the file downloaded from the gist; the issue says the two checkers share an author and the certificate format, which also made the certificate. The source states the certificate is a dilation of a binary64 packing made with Daniel's search/packer/dilate_cert.py, delta 1e-12, on macOS arm64 with Python 3.14.6; it certifies the upper bound only and states no exact KKT solve, local-optimality or rigidity analysis. It calls the packing a new packing of another lineage than Francisco Couzo's at 344: the register's 307 record design (Nate Chaoweeraprasit / PingYou Ltd, PR #574) stretched one K-step and polished. Those are the source's statements. No source program ran here.
register.credit: Credit Amund Kristiansen (https://gist.github.com/amundsk/18ada41ec384b6ff2c96f58b7ce7d1a6), whose search stretched the register's 307 record design (Nate Chaoweeraprasit (itsnaka), with PingYou Ltd's certificate, PR #574) by one K-step, started from 307 minima of that design and polished in float32 GPU batches with Evan Daniel's fq quench, as the issue says; the certificate was made with Daniel's dilate_cert.py and checked with his checkers. The search, the certificate and the request were done by Claude (Anthropic) in Claude Code at Amund Kristiansen's direction.
